Cold-rich bypass ratio, stripper pressure, and stripper steam flow were held constant. The capture efficiency and SRD varied with changing solvent flow rate. The stripper sump temperature varied when steam flow was held constant while the solvent flow rate changed. The objective was to find the maximum capture efficiency. ION was able to manipulate the L/G ratio with significantly more accuracy than during the MEA campaign as there was no foaming with ICE-21™. However, inconsistent Gasmet CO measurement accuracy resulted in poor overall data quality due to poor mass balance 2 closure. ION switched to a different CO measurement for the ICE-31® campaign (described further 2 in the Section 8). 7.2.2 Steam Turndown The flue gas flow rate and temperature were held constant. The solvent flow rate was varied to achieve the desired capture efficiency. Cold-rich bypass flow was held relatively constant. Stripper pressure was held constant. Stripper steam flow was allowed to vary to maintain constant sump temperature. The objective was to determine the SRD as solvent flow rate was changed to achieve specified capture efficiencies. ION did not perform this work package due to time and flue gas availability constraints in the ICE-21™ campaign. 7.2.3 Flue Gas Turndown ION operated the system with varying flue gas flow rates. Flue gas temperature was held constant, as was solvent flow rate, cold-rich bypass ratio, and stripper pressure. Stripper sump temperature varied slightly. The capture efficiency and SRD varied as dependent variables. The objective was to evaluate turndown performance with ICE-21™. In theory, maintaining solvent flow rate and steam flow constant while reducing flue gas flow rate should result in a measurable increase in capture efficiency and SRD. 7.2.4 Flue Gas Temperature The flue gas flow rate was held constant. The flue gas temperature was varied in order to determine the change in SRD when capture efficiency is held constant. All system parameters were held constant except solvent flow rate and stripper temperature (and thus steam); these two ION Clean Energy 18 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT parameters were varied as needed to maintain capture efficiency at nominally 95%. Due to lack of DCC blowdown during the ICE-21™ campaign, flue gas temperature was not controllable, and this work package could not be completed. 7.2.5 Long-Term Testing The system was operated with ICE-21™ at the most optimal conditions as determined through the various work packages performed during parametric testing. Optimal process conditions varied due to the changing concentration of CO in the inlet flue gas. ION operators manipulated process 2 parameters to target 95-96% capture efficiency, which is the optimal operating window for the capture system. 7.3 Work Package 3 – ICE-31® Parametric Testing 7.3.1 Flue Gas Temperature The flue gas flow rate was held constant. The flue gas temperature was varied to determine the change in SRD when capture efficiency was held constant.
